name: Gilt market
summary: Long gilt yields near multi-decade highs: 10y near 5.3% and 30y 5.77% on 19 Nov, with a December rate rise priced
state: The 10-year gilt yield was little changed near 5.3% on 19 Nov, having eased from a one-month high above 5.35% on 16 Nov after October CPI of 3.6% came in slightly below forecast (Trading Economics). The 30-year yield was 5.77% on 19 Nov, 9bp lower over a month but close to the highest levels since 1998 reached in October (Trading Economics; Reuters via The Edge). Markets price about an 80% chance of a December Bank Rate rise. The 10-year's monthly move is inside the 40bp line, and Watch is kept because long yields remain near multi-decade highs.
for_you: Mortgage and other borrowing rates tend to follow gilt yields, so households with fixed-rate deals coming up for renewal are exposed to higher costs. Annuity and pension pricing is also sensitive to long gilt yields.
rubric_hit: Watch: 30y gilt near multi-decade highs (5.77% on 19 Nov); 10y monthly move under 40bp; no BoE intervention

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
